fields.reasoning: Routes and their order come from internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml's on.* targets and comments, its conduct handback template (spawn the role, never fix it yourself), the handback.md shape in internal/run/brief.go, and the gate-fix, ci-fix and conflict-fix topics' own scopes; rhiza check and signoff have no dedicated fixer role, so the generic fixer takes them, as the fixer topic fixes findings given in its prompt. A wait-ci timeout means CI never settled (a red CI settles the wait and fails at merge), so ci-fix, which reproduces the tests and findings of rhiza ship check --json, has nothing to act on and the timeout gets no fixer.
fields.statement: A conductor handed back by ship-change reads handback.md (Failing step, Outcome, Failing commands with their kept output, Output tail, Cause, Failed CI runs, Conflicted files) and spawns, never fixes: gate's rhiza run build-check a verifier for the leaf lacking independent Evidence (a builder retry if it fails); gate's rhiza run review-check a critic for the check with an open blocker or major, then a fixer for confirmed findings and the checks again; gate's rhiza check a fixer with the output as its findings; gate's rhiza ship gate and the push step's rhiza ship open-pr (its pre-push check) the gate-fix role; signoff changes a fixer with the owner's requested changes, then the checks; merge's settled red CI the ci-fix role; wait-ci's timeout spawns no role, since CI never settled and there are no failing tests or findings to fix: the conductor reads rhiza ship check --json, changes nothing and finishes, so the run goes through gate, signoff, push and a fresh CI wait, and a CI that never settles parks at handback_cap; merge's conflicting PR or moved main rhiza ship rebase --no-push (never plain ship rebase), then the conflict-fix role for a code conflict it leaves; every route lands and renders again, then rhiza session done. After handback_cap hand-backs (3 unless set) the next red parks the run stopped with an inbox item, and the steps after the merge never hand back.
fields.wording: Hand-back routes as ship-change and the fixer role topics give them (derived from the code, autonomous plan run)

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/guide -run 'TestConductHandback|TestConduct|TestList' shows the conduct-handback topic listed and under TopicCap, the conduct topic's Read first naming rhiza guide conduct-handback and staying under TopicCap, and conduct-handback naming handback.md's section titles as internal/run/brief.go renders them (Failing step, Outcome, Failing commands, Output tail, Cause, Failed CI runs, Conflicted files), rhiza run build-check, rhiza run review-check, rhiza check, rhiza ship gate, rhiza ship open-pr, rhiza ship rebase --no-push, the roles verifier, critic, fixer, gate-fix, ci-fix and conflict-fix, handback_cap and rhiza session done; the test parses the built-in ship-change with the workflow package and requires the topic to name every step whose on.* target is handback:conduct and every command of its gate step; (failure case) the test fails naming the step or command when ship-change hands back from a step, or its gate runs a command, the topic does not name, and the topic's Routes section (one entry per hand-back step) naming a step whose on.* targets include no handback:conduct (main-ci, close-out, ship, deploy-check, derived from the parsed ship-change) as a route fails it naming that step; the wait-ci route naming the ci-fix role fails it; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/guide passes.
fields.files: internal/guide/text/conduct-handback.md, internal/guide/conduct_handback_test.go, internal/guide/guide.go, internal/guide/guide_test.go, internal/guide/text/conduct.md, internal/guide/conduct_test.go, cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/guide.txtar
fields.must_not: Change the hand-back mechanism, handback.md's rendering, ship-change.toml or any fixer role topic: guide text and its tests only; grow the conduct topic past TopicCap; tell the conductor to fix anything itself
fields.statement: The guide has a conduct-handback topic, named in the conduct topic's Read first, giving the shape of handback.md (Failing step, Outcome, Failing commands with output paths, Output tail, Cause, Failed CI runs, Conflicted files) and, for each step of the conductor default ship-change that hands back to conduct, the route a conductor takes as conduct-handback-routes decides: the gate's four commands, signoff changes, push, wait-ci's timeout and merge (CI red, conflicting PR, moved main via rhiza ship rebase --no-push), each by spawning the named role, then land, render and rhiza session done; plus handback_cap and that the steps after the merge never hand back.
